Compared the complete original lem:uniformrot at source lines 428-453, both numbered clauses and both sign orientations of each, with SM.uniform_rotation and the actual geometric definitions and proof bodies in DirectionProjection, CumulativeTurns, NarrowSector, UniformRotation and the inherited regular/rotation/reversal modules. The source-facing aggregate retains n>=3, the actual labelled planar tuple P, Regular P, and the explicit premise that every actual turn is nonzero. The additional NeZero n instance is redundant under n>=3. The domain is the source regular locus, not a stronger generic or embedded-polygon locus: no globally distinct vertices, no-self-crossing, chirotope genericity, supplied sector, chosen unwrapped argument, or desired rotation inequality is assumed. The source's left and right turns are exactly turn P i=1 and turn P i=-1 with the already reviewed determinant convention. The aggregate has four separate conclusions: all left implies rotation at least 1; all right implies rotation at most -1; one right with all other labels left implies rotation at least 1; and one left with all other labels right implies rotation at most -1. The existential exceptional-index encodings express exactly one opposite turn, because every other index is required to have the other, distinct sign. None of these four clauses is omitted or certified only conditionally on another unproved uniform-rotation claim.

The inherited rotationNumber is the actual sum of principal turns divided by 2*pi, and rotationNumber_integer is the previously reviewed geometric theorem, not an axiom or a premise supplied to this result. principalTurn_sign identifies the sign of the actual principal angle with the source turn. After strict positivity of rotation is proved, rotationNumber_ge_one_of_pos uses the genuine integer witness to obtain the bound 1<=rotation. This preserves the source normalization and sign.

The hard positive argument is fully reconstructed from actual edge directions and closure. turnPrefix P k is the real sum of the principal turns at the successive labels 1 through k, starting from edge 0. Its direction identity is established in the genuine Real.Angle quotient of period 2*pi: every summand is the difference of the adjacent actual edge-direction classes, and finite telescoping gives the class of the prefix as the class of arg(edge k)-arg(edge 0). No equality of unwrapped real edge arguments is assumed. The finite cyclic index set is compared with natural representatives through the actual Fin/ZMod equivalence. sum_principalTurn_eq_prefix proves that the full actual turn sum is the prefix through n-1 plus the turn at label 0. The nonzero natural-index lemma explicitly checks 1<=j<n, so prefix positivity and monotonicity do not accidentally include the exceptional label or a wrapped copy of it. For every actual edge index i, the prefix at i.val lies between zero and the full positive prefix.

Under a contradiction assumption rotation<=0, the sum decomposition and the strict regular bound principalTurn P 0>-pi imply that the full positive prefix L is strictly less than pi. Regularity supplies exactly this bound; no strict sign at the exceptional label is needed by the helper. DirectionProjection defines the concrete vector (cos a,sin a), with a=arg(edge 0)+L/2. Its dot product with an actual vector is proved in real coordinates to equal the actual Euclidean length times cos(arg(vector)-a), using the complex real/imaginary coordinate identities. The previously reviewed euclideanLength is the Euclidean square-root norm, not the product-space norm. The angle-class prefix identity is transferred only to cosine, a well-defined periodic function on Real.Angle. Therefore the projection for edge i equals its positive Euclidean length times cos(prefix(i.val)-L/2), even when individual complex arguments cross their principal branch cut. The prefix bounds and L<pi place that cosine argument strictly between -pi/2 and pi/2. The inspected Mathlib cosine-positivity theorem then gives a strictly positive actual dot product with every edge. This is an explicit geometric direction, not an assumed dual-cone or sector oracle.

Finally, planeDotAddHom and planeDot_sum prove additivity of this actual dot product over the finite edge sum. The inherited sum_edges theorem is the coordinate telescoping identity for the actual closed polygon. Strict positivity of all projections therefore makes a finite sum strictly positive, while edge closure forces it to equal the dot product with zero, a contradiction. All edge lengths used here are nonzero by Regular. The proof does not impose an immersion or no-crossing condition beyond the source's regularity. The helper consequently proves the stronger assertion that all turns away from one chosen cut being positive already force positive rotation. Using this valid stronger result does not alter the source-facing premises: SM.uniform_rotation explicitly retains the all-nonzero-turn hypothesis and, in the one-opposite cases, the prescribed sign at the exceptional index. The uniform positive case also follows from the same helper by taking any cut; it is not left as an unstated appeal to the printed source proof.

The exceptional index is transported correctly. shift a P has new turn i equal to old turn i+a, so an old exceptional label a becomes new label zero. The proof checks that i!=0 implies i+a!=a, uses actual regularity preservation under this shift, and transports the result back with the proved rotationNumber_shift identity. For both negative cases the actual reversal is P(2-i), preserves Regular, has turn(reversal P,i)=-turn(P,2-i), and negates the actual rotation number. An old exceptional index a becomes 2-a, and the proof explicitly verifies that every other reversed index maps to an old index different from a. Applying the established positive case to this actual reversed tuple gives exactly the required negative bound. This uses neither an incorrect plain negation of labels nor a silent identification of reversal with a cyclic shift. Uniform all-right and exactly-one-left are both included. These actual cyclic and reversal transports also supply the source's explicitly permitted labelled/equivariant interpretation without a distinguished polygon vertex.

The source hash, all 17 inspected local supporting-file hashes, and the independently recomputed semantic dependency hash match the passed checkpoint-023 development receipt. The four new modules are unchanged from this independent source/type/body review, and the thirteen inherited modules are byte-identical to earlier independent reviews. The receipt audits 791 project declarations and 19 mapped claims with only the standard propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound axioms and explicitly leaves stage_accepted false. This review certifies the complete original PROVE row lem:uniformrot only. It does not certify the later Whitney/shift statements, the corner state sum, or the main wall-crossing/soft-theorem targets. The projection, prefix and sector helpers are not counted as additional original claims. No Lean or declaration-map file was authored or edited by this reviewer.

SM.uniform_rotation (work/lean/SM/UniformRotation.lean:64-71) has hypotheses (hn : 3 <= n), (P : LabelledTuple n), (h : Regular P), (htau : forall i, turn P i != 0) and concludes the conjunction of exactly four implications: (forall i, turn P i = 1) -> 1 <= rotationNumber P; (forall i, turn P i = -1) -> rotationNumber P <= -1; (exists a, turn P a = -1 and forall i != a, turn P i = 1) -> 1 <= rotationNumber P; and the mirror with 1/-1 exchanged -> rotationNumber P <= -1. The existential encoding with all other indices forced to the opposite sign is exactly 'exactly one right, all others left'. Definitions denote the printed objects: LabelledTuple n = ZMod n -> R x R (Polygon.lean:14-15), the labelled-representative reading the source's formalization remark explicitly permits; edge P i = P(i+1) - P i = l_i (Polygon.lean:44); det u v = u1 v2 - u2 v1 (Polygon.lean:17); chi P i j k = sign det(P j - P i, P k - P i) and turn P i = chi P (i-1) i (i+1) in SignType with 1 = left, -1 = right (Chirotope.lean:10-14, matching def:chirotope and lem:chi-basic(iv)); Regular P = forall i, RegularPair (edge P (i-1)) (edge P i) with RegularPair u v = u != 0 and v != 0 and no r < 0 with v = r*u (RegularLocus.lean:12-13, RegularPairs.lean:8-9), exactly def:regular's R_n; principalTurn P i = arg(conj(l_{i-1}) * l_i) which under RegularPair lies in (-pi,pi) with cos = <u,v>/(|u||v|) and sign = sign det (RegularPairs.lean:54, PrincipalAngles.lean:9-12, RegularLocus.lean:15-16), i.e. the printed principal turn theta_i; rotationNumber P = (sum_i principalTurn P i)/(2 pi) (RotationNumber.lean:10-11) = rot(P). Same domain, hypotheses, quantifiers and conclusions; nothing vacuous (regular polygons with all turns nonzero exist). sm15_reworded is false, CHANGES_SINCE_20260909.md does not mention this lemma, and the SM15 excerpt is byte-identical to the SM12 excerpt; the accepted Lean statement matches the SM15 text.
